Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - Acute diarrhea for ~3 days.
  - No recent travel; no unusual or “dodgy” food reported. History of similar episodes after certain foods/travel in the past, but not with this episode.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - 4–5 bowel movements/day; consistency varies (sometimes watery, sometimes loose).
  - Mild abdominal pain.
  - One episode of vomiting.
  - Possible mild fever (patient unsure).
  - Decreased appetite but maintaining oral fluid intake.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable).
  - Not reported: no throat swelling/closure sensation, no voice change/hoarseness, no dysphagia/odynophagia, no drooling, no nasal/ocular symptoms, no stridor/noisy breathing, no dyspnea, no swelling of lips/tongue/uvula/face, no ear pain/hearing changes, no neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Occasional prior diarrhea after certain foods or travel (no specifics).
  - No prior hospital care or injection therapy for this issue mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: None reported.
  - Medications: Inhaler named “Laxepro/Lexapro” (patient reports yellow inhaler) for asthma—dose/route/frequency not documented. Conflict noted: Lexapro is typically an oral antidepressant, not an inhaler; medication name/type unclear.
  - No other prescription or OTC medications taken for current symptoms.
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Patient at a secure location; accompaniment not stated.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution.
  - No facial/oral/uvular/tongue swelling stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors.
  - No respiratory distress, stridor, or noisy breathing mentioned.
- Mental status and associated features.
  - Conversant and coherent; no dizziness/syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded. Clinician noted the patient “doesn’t look dehydrated” on video.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Acute non-bloody diarrhea with single vomiting episode, likely self-limited gastroenteritis; patient maintaining oral fluids and appears not dehydrated by clinician observation. No ENT involvement or red flag airway symptoms reported.
- Past medical history notable for asthma; inhaler identity uncertain (conflict noted regarding “Laxepro/Lexapro,” yellow inhaler vs typical Lexapro tablet).
- Family history: Father had/has hypertension (conflict noted) and died of bowel cancer at age 62 (10 years ago).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised.
  - Supportive care: maintain high oral fluid intake.
  - Oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) OTC recommended.
  - Dietary advice: soft/bland diet (e.g., toast, crackers, simple foods); avoid dairy, meat, fish, and eggs during active diarrhea. Use yogurt/probiotics to help restore gut flora.
  - Gradual reintroduction: after 48 hours without diarrhea, may slowly reintroduce boiled/mashed vegetables and then meat/eggs/fish.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver.
  - Review written advice in the app.
  - Contact the clinic if needing clarification or if symptoms persist/worsen.
- Escalation criteria/red flags.
  - Seek care if bowel movements increase to ≥6–8/day, signs of dehydration develop, diarrhea persists beyond 1 week, or blood/mucus appears in stool.
  - If blood in stool occurs, a stool sample will be needed; antibiotics may be considered depending on results.
  - Hospital evaluation advised if significant dehydration is suspected.
- Follow-up.
  - Return/telehealth follow-up if no improvement or if red flags occur.
  - Consider clarifying asthma medication name/type and usage at next contact.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements for an acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  - Detailed ENT review (throat exam, oropharyngeal findings) and vitals not recorded.
  - No documentation of airway assessment beyond symptom inquiry.
  - No medication dose/route/frequency for inhaler; inhaler identity unclear.
  - No stool sample obtained at this time; no hydration status metrics (e.g., orthostatic symptoms, urine output) documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Inhaler name reported as “Laxepro/Lexapro,” yellow inhaler; Lexapro is generally an oral antidepressant (not an inhaler). Conflict noted.
  - Family history phrasing: “has” vs “had” hypertension in father who died 10 years ago. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional brief audio clarity issues requiring repetition.
